citations.assessment: Yose in Shimon Shezuri’s name distinguishes beans rooting in two separate years, and the later clause discusses Shmuel’s ruling.
The Tosefta explicitly names both and continues to the proposed gathering and designation of produce.
Dostai and Yose occur in adjacent statements about the animal enclosure, with Yose’s statement in Rabbi Eliezer’s name. This gives the relation in the legal discussion.
The checked Bavli has Rabbi Elazar without patronymic. The exact Sifrei parallel explicitly writes Elazar ben Azaryah and gives the same distinction between remarriage and betrothal.

The Bavli explicitly sends Yose and the grandson of Zekharyah ben Kevutal. The Yerushalmi’s related account gives Yitzchak and Natan as the letter-bearers. Preserve the two envoy accounts.

citations.assessment: The Bavli explicitly gives Rabbi Eliezer and the rule on thirty elapsed days of the twentieth year.
Chapter 1 names Rabbi Eliezer for the irrigation report. Chapter 2 names him in the animal-enclosure report. Compare the version of the irrigation teaching in the Yerushalmi separately.
Directly names Yose ben Kipper expounding in Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua's name about prohibited relationships and exceptions.
The Guggenheimer numbering places the parallel irrigation clause at 2:3:5, naming Yose ben Kofer and Elazar ben Shammua. The received 2:4 leads to a distinct discussion in this edition.

citations.assessment: The checked Bavli pairs Yose with Dostai bar Yannai on Ahai’s errand. Dostai be-Rabbi Yehudah appears in a different Tosefta notice.
Gittin directly has Ahai send Yose and Dostai bar Yannai to retrieve his deposited silver vessel. No relationship beyond the episode is inferred.
The target specifies that the envoy was Zekharyah’s grandson.
The companion section gives the intercalation narrative. It tracks the Yerushalmi’s different envoy names without collapsing the versions.
